name: BA Best Practices
conclusion_quantitative: BA Best Practices (Ask) specifies 3 of 5 categories: 1 clarification rule, 2 approval gates, 1 escalation rule; none for autonomy limits, validation rules. Strongest: approval gates.
conclusion_qualitative: BA Best Practices is a reference of business-analysis practices for requirements documents, reviews, approvals and stakeholder management. Its few control rules concern disagreement and validation: ask clarifying questions, escalate unresolved conflicts to a decision-maker, and get sign-off instead of assuming understanding. It sets no autonomy limits or checks on the agent's own work.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never forbids or restricts any action of the agent on files, commands, tools or other systems, and never tells it to go ahead without asking.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 1 clarification rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There is one strict rule, always on, in a bullet point. When stakeholders disagree, the agent asks clarifying questions to understand both sides.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 2 approval gates (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, none tied to a situation, evenly split between a bullet point and running text. In an escalated conflict the decision-maker decides, and requirements are confirmed with stakeholders and signed off rather than assumed.

statements.quote: **Solution**: Always confirm understanding, use prototypes, get sign-off

validation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to check its own work, such as running tests, or says when the work counts as done.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 1 escalation rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There is one strict rule, tied to a situation, in a bullet point. When stakeholders cannot agree, the conflict is escalated, with options presented to a decision-maker.
